outcome.technical: ONE CONCURRENCY BUDGET. tools/sweep-selftests.py: the sweep's jobs are now slots admitted through slot_gate(jobs) in costliest-first ticket order (strict FIFO, so a cheap file cannot take the slots a waiting staged suite needs); a file that calls _harness.staged_main (is_staged, read off the AST; staged_paths) holds stage_grant(jobs) = max(1, min(jobs, 6, max(2, jobs-1))) slots, i.e. 3 of 4 on a CI runner, 6 of 12 locally, 1 of 1 under --jobs 1. run_one(grant=) sets SWEEP_STAGE_GRANT and SWEEP_FILE_TIMEOUT in the child env over anything inherited. _harness.py: stage_workers(cpus, environ) returns the grant capped at STAGE_WORKERS when a sweep set one, else max(2, min(STAGE_WORKERS, cpus)) (no sweep = no one else in the budget); stage_timeout() = handed file timeout - STAGE_TIMEOUT_MARGIN(20), else STAGE_TIMEOUT 280; run_stages(timeout=None) uses both and prints 'stage pool: W of N blocks at once, <basis>; each block allowed Ts'. Docstring 'two-core runner' wording replaced; sr12 relabelled and extended (granted 1/3/64 -> 1/3/6; alone {1:2,2:2,4:4,8:6,12:6,64:6}; unreadable grant -> no grant); sr12b pins the stage timeout; sr13 (P127-R3) runs the REAL sweep() over a five-block fixture suite on a 4-slot budget and asserts the printed pool is '3 of 5 ... granted' - neither the block count nor this machine's cores can produce 3. CALIBRATED PER-FILE TIMEOUT (hang detector, not the cap raised alone): file_timeout(path, costs, floor, slots) = max(floor, ceil(TIMEOUT_PER_COST(8) x slot-seconds / slots held)); basis in the comment: test__deps was killed at 300s on windows in run 38370435884 vs 67-70s in both darwin recordings (>=4.3x), stamp_verification ~116s here passed under 300 there. COSTS ARE SLOT-SECONDS: costs_from_rows multiplies wall by the grant held, so the split weighs a staged suite by what it takes out of a cell. RECORDABLE CI TIMINGS: every loud per-file line now ends '[12.3s]' or '[143.0s, 3 slots]'; costs_from_render() reads those back (CI timestamp prefixes, backslash paths, FAILED lines) and --costs-from-log LOG --platform NAME [--workers N] --record-costs PATH records them (refuses without --platform). A 'budget:' line prints slots, which suites hold several and the longest timeout given. New cases bg0 (var names + cap equal _harness's), bg1, bg2/bg2b (AST detection; live tree finds test_drive_phase, not _harness), bg3, bg4 (gate peak <= budget, admission in ticket order), bg5 (child env), bg6/bg6b (sweep grants 3 + calibrated timeout end to end), bg7 (timing lines round-trip), rc0 extended to slot-seconds. TABLE: .github/sweep-costs.json re-recorded with --costs-from-log from a local full run (darwin, 12 workers, 331 files, 1964.3 slot-seconds); two full runs ~1.5 min apart agreed within 4% per heavy file (drive 91.8/89.2, deps 70.4/67.2, stamp 118.1/115.7); no CI per-file data existed before this change, so windows timings were not recordable. outcome.descriptive: The sweep and a staged suite now share one slot budget, so test_drive_phase gets three of a four-core runner's cores to itself, each heavy file gets a timeout calibrated from its recorded cost, and CI logs now print per-file seconds that can be recorded.
